This chunk is about:
- Organizations: Centre for Medieval and Renaissance Studies, St. Olaf College
- People: Michael Bauman, Bernt Julius Muus, Thorbjorn N. Mohn
- Places: Oxford
- Topics: American colleges and universities connected to CMRS

Facts:
- St. Olaf College was founded in 1874 by a group of Norwegian-American immigrant pastors and farmers led by Pastor Bernt Julius Muus.
- Thorbjorn N. Mohn, who lived from July 15, 1844 to November 18, 1899, was an American Lutheran church leader and the first president of St. Olaf College.
- Michael Bauman served for eight years as Lecturer and Tutor in Renaissance theology and literature at the Centre for Medieval and Renaissance Studies in Oxford.
- Michael Bauman also served as Associate Dean of the Summer School at the Centre for Medieval and Renaissance Studies in Oxford.
- The Centre for Medieval and Renaissance Studies received students from American colleges and universities including the University of Georgia, Elmhurst College, St. Mary's College of California, St. Mary's College of Maryland, St. Olaf College, William Jewell College, and Middlebury College.
